---
id: "smk-02"
title: "Python (programming language)"
---

Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. Its design emphasises code readability, using indentation rather than braces to delimit blocks, and it supports several programming paradigms, including procedural, object-oriented and functional styles. Python is dynamically typed and garbage-collected, and its reference implementation, CPython, compiles source code to bytecode that is executed by a virtual machine. The language ships with a large standard library, and an even larger ecosystem of third-party packages is distributed through the Python Package Index. Python is widely used for web development, scripting, data analysis, scientific computing and machine learning. Development is coordinated by the Python Software Foundation, and language changes are proposed and discussed in numbered documents called Python Enhancement Proposals. Python 3, released in 2008, introduced changes that were not backward compatible with Python 2.
